items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good gaming YouTube video introducing the two main characters of the game GTA 6, Jason and Lucia, and the people around them. The Narrator is THRILLED and grinning the whole time: an excited, fun friend who has studied every trailer and can't wait to tell you who these characters are. A huge smile you can hear in every line, bright and upbeat, warm and natural like real excited conversation, never like reading a script. Wide, lively pitch movement; real amazement on every number and reveal; playful laughter in the voice on the funny bits (a private browser tab, Rockstar wrote that not me, the landlord). A sly, teasing, conspiratorial grin on the theory about Brian. Punch the key words with energy. Short lines like 'Jason and Lucia.', 'Number one. Cal Hampton.', 'Other people. Like Jason.' are crisp labels with a beat after them. Pace quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never flat, calm, sleepy, monotone or documentary-serious, and never shouty or fake. Keep exactly the same pace and energy in the last minute as in the first. Accent: native General American English, neutral American accent from first word to last. VOICE IDENTITY: the same person and the same high energy from the first line to the last. Say 'GTA 6' as the letters G, T, A then 'six', and 'GTA' as the letters G, T, A. Pronounce 'Leonida' as 'lee-oh-NEE-dah', 'Lucia' as 'loo-SEE-ah', 'Caminos' as 'kah-MEE-nohs', 'Duval' as 'doo-VAHL', 'Dre'Quan' as 'DRAY-kwahn', 'Raul Bautista' as 'rah-OOL bow-TEES-tah', 'Heder' as 'HEE-der', 'Boobie Ike' as 'BOO-bee eyek', 'Real Dimez' as 'real dimes', 'Bae-Luxe' as 'bay lux', 'DWNPLY' as the single word 'downplay'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word: stop right after the final sentence and never add, invent or continue with any words of your own. The text is given one sentence group per line: read every line in order, do not skip any line.
lines: Thirteen years. That's how long we waited for this game. And now you're about to spend a hundred hours with two people you barely know.
So before you press start, let's fix that.
I went through everything Rockstar has officially shown. Every trailer, every character page, and the full Extended Look. No leaks. No spoilers.
I'll show you who these two really are, who the six people around them are, and how playing as a couple actually works.
And at the end, I'll tell you which one of their so-called friends I don't trust. At all.
Welcome to Five Star Intel. Let's go!
Rockstar sums him up in one line. Jason wants an easy life, but things just keep getting harder.
He grew up around grifters and crooks. He joined the Army to shake off a rough start, and in the launch trailer, he admits he got into trouble there too.
So now he's down in the Leonida Keys, doing the one thing he knows. Working for local drug runners.
He even lives rent free, in a house his boss owns. All he has to do is help with a few shakedowns. Remember that boss. He comes back later.
Jason isn't a kingpin. He isn't a psycho. He's a guy who's good at bad work, and he's tired of it.
Then he meets Lucia. And Rockstar's own words are, it could be the best, or the worst thing that ever happened to him.
Her dad taught her to fight as soon as she could walk. And life has been swinging at her ever since.
She fought for her family, and that fight landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. That's the prison from the very first trailer.
She only got out through sheer luck. And in the trailers, you can still spot the ankle monitor on her leg.
Trailer two even opens with Jason driving out to pick her up, the day she walks free.
But here's the thing about Lucia. She learned her lesson. From now on, only smart moves.
She wants the good life her mom has dreamed about since their days in Liberty City. Yes, that Liberty City.
And she is not waiting for anyone to hand it to her.
She's also making history. Lucia is the first woman to lead a modern GTA story.
So put them together. He wants easy. She wants out. And Rockstar says a life with Jason could be her way out.
Then one easy score goes wrong. And suddenly these two are in the middle of a criminal conspiracy that stretches across the whole state.
Rockstar's line for it is perfect. The darkest side of the sunniest place in America.
Now, how do you actually play as two people?
The Extended Look answers a lot. You can play as Jason. You can play as Lucia. And you can roam Leonida together, as a couple.
One of you drives, the other leans out and shoots. And the partner you're not controlling doesn't just stand there. They fight.
There are tiny details too. Walk side by side, and a prompt pops up to hold hands. Partner taking too long? There's a button to hurry them up.
They share an apartment. You pick outfits, raid the fridge, watch TV, and the other one is right there with you.
Previews go even further. They say your texts, and even how long you stay away from home, can change the relationship. We'll test that ourselves.
And previews say the way they live shows up on their bodies. Hit the gym, and they build muscle. Eat too much, or skip sleep, and you'll see that too. Very San Andreas.
Okay. Now the six people around them. And this is where it gets good.
Cal is Jason's friend, and he works for the same boss. He's also deep, deep into online conspiracies.
His idea of a great night is a few beers, the Coast Guard radio, and a private browser tab. Rockstar wrote that, not me.
His official quote? What if everything on the internet was true? That tells you everything about Cal.
Cal is happy right where he is. Jason wants more. Watch that gap.
A Vice City legend who turned his time on the streets into a legit empire. Real estate, a strip club, and a recording studio.
Boobie is all smiles. Until it's time to talk business.
More of a hustler than a gangster. He sold on the street to get by, but music was always the dream.
Now he runs a label called Only Raw Records, with Boobie as his partner. And they badly need a hit.
Number four is actually two people. Real Dimez.
Bae-Luxe and Roxy. Friends since high school, who went from shaking down dealers to making rap and blowing up online.
Their first track, with a local rapper called DWNPLY, was a hit. But that was five years ago. Now they have a fresh deal, and one more shot.
Dre'Quan signed them. Boobie's club books them. See how those three connect? That's a whole storyline, sitting right there.
A veteran bank robber with confidence, charm, and cunning. He's always hunting for new talent that's ready to take big risks.
But Rockstar adds a warning. His recklessness raises the stakes on every single score.
So when Jason and Lucia join his crew, it's level up, or get out.
And number six. Brian Heder. Jason's boss. The landlord.
Brian is a classic drug runner from the golden age of smuggling in the Keys. He still moves product through his boat yard, with his third wife, Lori.
And here's the line that got me. Brian has been around long enough to let other people do his dirty work.
So here's my theory. And this is just me, not Rockstar.
That free house isn't a gift. It's a leash. Jason takes the risk, Brian keeps the profit. And when that easy score goes wrong, guess who's standing right in front of it?
I could be completely wrong. But I'm keeping both eyes on Brian.
And look at the map while you're at it. Jason's world is the Keys. Boobie's world is Vice City. Raul robs banks. Somehow, one story has to tie all of that together.
Now, what don't we know? Rockstar hasn't shown how this story ends, how long it runs, or whether Jason and Lucia make it out together.
And honestly? Good. I want to find that out with a controller in my hands.
So. Jason wants an easy life. Lucia wants a better one. And the six people around them all want something too.
Tell me in the comments. Are you playing as Jason first, or Lucia? And who don't you trust?
If this helped, subscribe to Five Star Intel. We're covering this game every week. See you in Leonida!
